definition: Complacent means so self-satisfied and unconcerned that you no longer watch for danger or shortcomings.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word complacent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know complacent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Years of easy approvals left the loan office complacent, and nobody questioned the forged signatures until the third default.
Content is the harmless, milder cousin of complacent — a content baker is happy with the day's bread and still tastes every batch, while a complacent one is sure of the bread and has stopped tasting.
Heedless goes further than content—the heedless driver isn't even glancing at the gauges, while the complacent one glances and assumes they'll hold.

Smug is satisfaction worn where everyone can see it — the raised eyebrow, the little victory lap. Complacent satisfaction is quieter and more dangerous: the complacent have stopped checking for trouble, and the blindness matters more than the glow. Smug is a look you give others; complacent is a watch you've stopped keeping.

Self-satisfied means content with your own performance, deserved or not — a verdict you pass on yourself. Complacent adds the cost: the complacent are so settled in that satisfaction that they no longer watch for danger or shortcomings. You can be self-satisfied about yesterday; complacency is about what you miss tomorrow.

Complacent means so self-satisfied and unconcerned that you no longer watch for danger or shortcomings.
The orchard never sprayed for beetles because 'they'd never crossed the river'—a complacent bet that held right up until the summer the wind changed and half the crop was lost.
Complacent is sharper than 'relaxed' or 'confident' because it smuggles in a warning: the satisfaction is blind.
A confident team knows its strengths; a complacent one has stopped checking whether those strengths still exist.
Complacent always carries a hidden 'too': too satisfied, too soon, with a blind spot growing somewhere.
Don't use it for honest contentment—being content with a good harvest is healthy; being complacent about next year's beetles is how the harvest gets lost.

The inquiry into the Bay Belle's grounding opened with praise: thirty years of daily crossings without a single incident.
Then it turned to year thirty-one, when the crew had grown complacent.
The depth log was still filled in, the report noted, but from memory at the dock rather than from readings underway; the channel had always been where the channel had always been.
Nobody was lazy and nobody was reckless -- every sailor aboard believed the checks were being done, because for decades they always had been.
The sandbar that finally caught the hull had been building for three seasons, visible to anyone who still looked.
